name: gas_engine_complete_model
title: Complete gas engine: throttle, carburettor, combustion, cooling and recovery circuits
summary: Steady-state model of the 5 L four-stroke natural-gas engine of the ULiege MSTh course at its maximum-power point (2400 rpm, shaft power solved from the indicated efficiency): butterfly valve and carburettor, intake pressure drop through the valve area, adiabatic combustion chamber with the cpbar mean specific heat, expansion, jacket and water-to-environment exchangers, and two recovery exchangers (exercise 5). The stand-by throttling pressure drop is read in an engine map (external lookup table recovered from the sibling file TM-0137).
language_features: INTERPOLATE (native EES call form with a named argument)
user-library routine cpbar (implicit library, copied; function-position calls in the native file, CALL form in the variant)

authors: ULiège MSTh course (J. Lebrun, V. Lemort, S. Bertagnolio)
origin.course: Machines et systèmes thermiques (ULiège), repetition TP 08, exercises 1-5

verification.reference: EES stored solution of the original (97 common variables; the 98th, m, is a phantom variable of the original with an empty stored value), compared for the runnable _coolsolve variant with tools/compare_solution.py
verification.notes: 97 common variables, 6 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 9 (the constant PI and the 8 unused cpbar outputs). Excluding s_2 (absolute air entropy, CoolProp reference-state offset; its differences agree to 6e-5), the maximum is 9.4e-3 on cp_f = CP(CH4) (EES ideal-gas vs CoolProp real-fluid heat capacity, same deviation as CSL-0034). All other deviations explained in the README (cp_p_67 1.6e-3, W_dot_pumping 2.6e-3 on a small difference of two large pressures, Q_dot_recup_1 1.3e-3 on a 2.2 K temperature difference).
